result:
Done. Final state verified — here's the report.

## The idea

**Two pendulum bobs drive two pens across a page, and the time is the ink they leave** — every numeral a single plotted line that rings and loops at each corner because the pen overshoots, the whole drawing swaying with the bobs; each minute the changed numeral is reeled back up into the pen and inked in afresh.

## Process — the three pitches I weighed

| Pitch | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Harmonograph** — the time is the damped trace of two pendulums; strokes ring, corners overshoot, each minute the changed numeral is re-wound into the pen | **chosen** — the mechanism has a direct, controllable grip on letterform geometry, and it's a real machine, not a style |
| **Seismograph** — a drum advances under a stylus and the seismogram's envelope spells the digits | rejected: "waveform shaped like letters" is a well-worn trick, and reading it needs a huge trace |
| **Cloud chamber** — digits condense out of particle tracks curving in a magnetic field | rejected: gorgeous mood, but the tracks can't be made to read as a numeral at 1x |

Rejected inside the winner: a *sinusoidal ripple along each stroke* (reads as badly-drawn, not ringing), *corner loops on a wavy line* (mush), *faint echo passes* (blurred the glyphs), and a *dither halo for wet ink* (fuzz, not glow). Kept: **overshoot at the corners** as the letterform's signature, and wet ink as a slight thickening.

## Artifacts (`.claude/skills/oled-clock/`)

- `out/harmonograph-ds-digits.png` — all ten numerals at 8×, iterated three times
- `out/harmonograph-ds.png` — 10:09:30
- `out/harmonograph-ds-turn.png` — sheet across 10:09:58 (the unit digit is inked first, then the tens)
- `out/harmonograph-ds-hour.png` — sheet across 10:59:58 (all four churn, the sheet lurches)
- `out/harmonograph-ds.gif`, `out/harmonograph-ds-hour.gif` — 50 fps

## Check

```
node tools/check.mjs --design harmonograph-ds
  frames checked            : 20160
  worst frame               : 0.83 ms, 1024 RAM bytes  -> bus allows 1211 fps
  frames over the bus budget: 0     WARNING: none     ERROR: none
  pixels lit, on average    : 10.9% of the glass
  hottest pixel             : 12.9 h/day -> ~3.4 years to 50% at full contrast
  PASS
```
`frame()` averages **0.80 ms** (worst 6.6 ms, ~0.7% of frames over 3 ms). It was 6.9 ms until I replaced per-segment `thickLine` with a direct buffer plotter and took the allocations out of the path.

## The honest weakest point

**The layout is still, at bottom, a row of four numerals with a machine above it.** I know it, and I tried the obvious fix — moving the rig into the gap between the hours and the minutes so its two bobs *were* the colon. It rendered as a crane hook: two long rods converging on a small gap, and the "colon" stopped reading as a colon. I reverted. The mechanism is genuinely coupled to the ink (the bobs' angles literally set the sway, the per-pair pens have their own tours, the wet trail tracks each pen), so it isn't decoration — but the composition is conventional in a way the concept isn't.

Two smaller ones: at exactly `sec = 0.00` the old value is still on the glass for a single frame before the rewind bites (every animated design here does this, but it is a wrong-time frame); and the corner overshoots, the thing that makes the letterform *this* letterform, are only ~3 px — you see them at 1×, but they're a whisper rather than the shout I wanted.

*(Unrelated: `automaton`, `automaton-opus5` and `fireworks` are failing to load in `sim/designs/index.js` from other work in the tree — I left them alone.)*
